definition: In natural language processing, Witten-Bell discounting is a method that can address the sparse data and zero-frequency issues in N-gram algorithms.
details: It was first proposed by Ian Witten and Tim Bell in 1991. A word that hasn't been encountered before is considered unseen, thus zero-frequency N-gram refers to an occurrence that has yet to take place; when it does, it will mark the initial instance we observe this new N-gram. Thus, the likelihood of encountering a zero-frequency N-gram can be represented by the likelihood of encountering an N-gram for the initial time. The idea behind Witten-Bell is the application of the number of items we have encountered once to assist in estimating the number of items never encountered. Utilizing this method, we can remove obtaining zero probability values for transition probability and maximum likelihood estimation for a series of words (N-gram) that is encountered for the first time in our algorithm.

explainer.lead: Witten–Bell discounting is a method in natural language processing that addresses sparse data and zero-frequency problems in N-gram algorithms. It matters because unseen N-grams otherwise get zero probability.

tiers.eli5: When you've never seen a particular word combination before, this method doesn't give it zero chance; it saves some probability for combinations it hasn't met yet.
tiers.practitioner: It is used to reassign probability mass from observed N-grams to unseen ones. A pitfall is forgetting that the estimate for a zero-frequency N-gram is tied to the chance of seeing an N-gram for the first time.
tiers.paperLevel: Proposed by Ian Witten and Tim Bell in 1991; an unseen word is zero-frequency, and the likelihood of encountering a zero-frequency N-gram is represented by the likelihood of encountering an N-gram for the first time, applying the number of items we have observed.

explainer.example: In an N-gram model, a combination never seen in training is assigned a small non-zero probability based on how often new N-grams have appeared.
